text:
anya: Heads-up — CI perf eval for rwd-v2-falcon-8q shows a ~28-35% p95 latency regression vs baseline after the quantization change. Dashboard spike around run 2025-11-03_03:12 UTC. Link: https://dash.redwood.ai/runs/2025-11-03/58123 :eyes:
perf-ci-bot: Automated summary: run_id=58123, model=rwd-v2-falcon-8q, quant=8-bit-ffd, concurrency_sweep=[1,8,32,128], p95_baseline=210ms, p95_current=278ms, cost_delta=+12%. Full artifacts: https://ci.artifacts/redwood/58123
samir: thanks, anya. Is the regression uniform across sequence lengths or only at long contexts?
anya: quick glance — 512 and 1024 both up. Short seq (64) looks fine. P95 jump is biggest at concurrency=32 and 128.
mike: could be batching/kv cache interaction with the quantized kernels. Did the runner change the batch_cutoff heuristics in the new release?
jess: I pushed a tweak two days ago to runner: optimize_batch_cutoff=true by default, aimed to reduce small-batch latency. @mike might be related.
samir: can we reproduce locally with the exact runner config the CI used? Share the run command and env from artifacts, please.
anya: pasted the runner args from artifact:
```
RWD_RUNNER_VERSION=2025.11.02-rc4
MODEL=rwd-v2-falcon-8q
QUANT_PROFILE=8-bit-ffd
CONCURRENCY=32
BATCH_CUTOFF_MS=8
ENABLE_PREFETCH=true
KV_CACHE_MODE=shared
```

mike: ok. two quick suspects: 1) prefetch causing head-of-line blocking at higher concurrency, 2) kernel fallback in quant path for sequence >512.
perf-ci-bot: Debug artifact: /artifacts/58123/kernels.log shows repeated fallback to slower GEMM on steps 210-260 for seq_len=1024.
anya: attaching a small log excerpt:
```
[2025-11-03T03:14:10Z] seq=1024 token_step=215 kernel=quant_attn -> fallback=gpu_gemm_slow (reason=blocked_optim)
[2025-11-03T03:14:10Z] seq=1024 token_step=216 kernel=quant_attn -> fallback=gpu_gemm_slow
```

samir: that matches. Fallbacks + prefetching can amplify latency under concurrency. Jess — can you try a quick run disabling prefetch and with batch_cutoff higher (e.g., 24ms) to see if p95 recovers?
jess: spawning a reproduce job now with two variants: (A) ENABLE_PREFETCH=false, BATCH_CUTOFF_MS=24; (B) ENABLE_PREFETCH=true, BATCH_CUTOFF_MS=24. I'll post results in ~12 min.
mike: also recommend rerunning with ENV DEBUG_KERNEL_SELECTION=1 to capture why quant_attn decided to fallback. That'll give us the exact condition.
anya: added a lightweight alert to the dashboard to mark baseline vs current for p95 so we don't miss recurring blips.
perf-ci-bot: reproduce jobs queued: job=58123-repro-A, job=58123-repro-B. ETA ~8-15m.
samir: if reproduce confirms it's kernel fallback, we may need to add a CI gating rule: quant profiles that trigger >5% fallback at typical seqs fail the binary quant rollout.
jess: repro-A finished: p95=225ms (concurrency=32), cost delta now +3%. Repro-B finished: p95=260ms.
anya: good signal — disabling prefetch helped a lot. Looks like prefetch + quant fallback interaction is the culprit.
mike: next steps: (1) add kernel selection logging in staging for a few hours, (2) adjust default batch_cutoff to 20ms for quantized models, (3) add CI check for fallback rate >5% at seq 512/1024.
samir: agreed. Jess, can you open a PR with the batch_cutoff change and a unit test that simulates fallback frequency? Put the PR into runner-config with a small rollout flag.
jess: on it. I'll include a short note for devex docs about the prefetch caveat for quant models.
anya: thanks everyone. tagging @mike for postmortem notes. :thumbsup:
mike: filing a short postmortem and adding an entry to perf runbook about "quantized kernel fallbacks + prefetch".
perf-ci-bot: Closing note: regression triaged -> mitigated (config tweak). Follow-ups: PR 4127 (runner batch cutoff), issue 2298 (kernel selection telemetry).
anya: filing a quick alert to ProdOps to avoid pushing 8q quant profile to Dedicated until PR lands.
samir: great work. we'll keep a close eye on next few CI sweeps. :eyes:
